warnings.why: Russia has historically very high tertiary attainment due to Soviet-era educational definitions, often mixing vocational and higher education in ways not directly comparable to ISCED short-cycle standards.
The reported 61.5 percent for short-cycle tertiary is exceptionally high for Central Asia and likely reflects a broad misclassification of upper secondary or vocational training.
Similar to Russia, the 60.7 percent rate is inflated by legacy post-secondary non-tertiary programs being counted as short-cycle tertiary.

policy: model memory is advisory; unsupported suspicions cannot overrule official data
